text:
nina: quick RFC follow-up: proposing a lightweight "live compaction shim" to tackle slow-build fragmentation from many tiny evicts. aim: reclaim slab space incrementally without pausing microbatches or regressing 99p latency. open to tradeoff suggestions.

sam: high-level: is this for steady drift fragmentation or batchy reclaim windows? what SLOs are we optimizing for?

nina: primarily steady drift + worst-case long-tail when we occasionally run full compaction. SLO target is keep 95/99 stable; allow small p50 blips during low utilization.
jules: how do we handle objects pinned by the KV cache or pinned tensors? moving live objects sounds risky.

nina: plan: shard-local coordinator picks candidate ranges, copies live objects to new slab pages in small quanta, publishes a lightweight remap table. reads consult remap table via a single indirection but only during an active compaction epoch. we apply remaps at microbatch safe points to minimize fast-path cost.
eric: indirection hurts. can we make remap lookups a single atomic read with no locks (e.g., a compact per-shard pointer table)? also need to avoid per-token overhead in generation hot path.
maria: suggestion: keep remap table in a small contiguous array; lookups are table[index] with atomic loads. we avoid per-object mutexes. also limit epoch duration and compress entries as ranges to reduce table size.
sam: correctness question: what if a microbatch spans the apply boundary? we need a bounded RCU-ish mechanism so in-flight requests see a consistent mapping.
jules: implement per-request epoch cookie: requests read current_epoch at start, and remap apply waits for inflight_count[current_epoch] to drop to zero before flipping epoch. similar to classic RCU but per-shard and bounded latency.
eric: when do we trigger compaction? fragmentation ratio alone is noisy. proposal: a small heuristic combining reclaimable_bytes/total_bytes > F and net_allocation_rate < A over a sliding 10s window. plus tenant gating.
maria: tenant gating is important. default: opt-out for premium tenants; standard tenants get auto compaction. and admin console needs per-shard policy: enabled, target_reclaim, quantum_ms, priority.
ops-bot: ops: perf job queued -> perf/compaction-live/epoch-probe (id: 4427)

nina: about remap overhead: we can publish diffs only and compress contiguous moves. quantum sizing (objects-per-step / quantum_ms) controls CPU vs reclaim throughput. prefer pulling back live objects from host-staging first to avoid double-copy.
sam: add a global latency-aware throttler: if observed 99th microbatch latency rises above threshold, reduce compaction rate or pause. token-bucket controlled by recent tail.
eric: tests: synthetic microbatch mixes with pinned-kv churn, measure p50/p95/p99, reclaimed bytes, remap-mem, CPU. also inject a microbatch that spans apply to validate RCU barrier.
jules: add a correctness checklist for race windows: remap atomicity, in-flight pointer stability, staged-page interactions. run fuzz tests that flip epoch at random times.
maria: UI: show compaction candidate shards, current reclaim%, estimated time to target, and option to force-run per-shard. also surface tenant gates and recent throttles.
nina: action items: I'll open a draft RFC PR with: handshake proto, remap table format, config schema, and perf matrix. tagging @sam @jules @eric @maria for review.
sam: +1. include a dev-flag to force-apply in staging.
jules: +1. please include small integration tests for host-offload path.
eric: ping me for perf runs once prototype is up.
